statuses.title: Return conservative privacy guarantees from Monte Carlo amplification
statuses.note: MC PLDs are built as simultaneous one-sided confidence bands: union-bounded Chernoff/KL lower CDF bound per rank with the unresolved residual pushed into infinity_mass, and a hard error if the band cannot meet the requested mc_resolution (balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:330-400); PLDs carry mc_resolution/mc_failure_probability/mc_confidence to Python (exposed on Pld). Python plumbing is conservative: epsilon_at clamps mc_resolution to delta/2 (_base.py:209-216), repeated_pld splits resolution as 1-(1-r)^(1/count) (_base.py:414-428), Composed.pld splits failure probability and resolution across groups (_composed.py:67-88), calibrate divides mc_failure_probability across probes and reports the overall value on CalibrateResult (calibration.py:296-325).

statuses.title: Reconcile negative-infinity mass in asymmetric PLD metrics
statuses.note: No commit in 79c916e3..4b13d82 changes how asymmetric metrics treat negative_infinity_mass (git log -S over pld/metrics.rs shows only #466, which exposes infinity_mass, and #283, docs/estimate labeling). The inconsistency named by the title persists: symmetric pmf_beta floors the CDF with negative_infinity_mass 'keeping beta estimates conservative' (metrics.rs:212-216), while pmf_beta_asymmetric explicitly renormalizes it away (metrics.rs:305,314 comments 'No negative_infinity_mass: it's absorbed by the renormalization'). Asymmetric PLDs with nonzero negative_infinity_mass are reachable (random_allocation.rs:157-185,250 and connect_the_dots.rs:278 both build new_asymmetric; composition adds left-tail budget to negative_infinity_mass in dense.rs). Magnitude is bounded by the tail budget so practical impact is tiny; the closure may have been a deliberate withdraw (GitHub unavailable to confirm), but nothing landed matching the title. Reported as a finding.

statuses.title: Remove latent sorted-sensitivity assumptions from MixtureConstants
statuses.note: MixtureConstants derives max_sensitivity/min_positive_sensitivity by order-independent folds (parallel_poisson.rs:143-153) and the inverse-loss bracket is built from those data-driven bounds with expansion loops (:192-246) - no code path indexes first/last as min/max. #592 pins delta for an explicitly unsorted, non-unit sensitivity vector against direct quadrature at 1e-10 for both adjacencies (test_mixture_delta_matches_quadrature_for_unsorted_nonunit_sensitivities). statuses.title: Make the linear-FFT safety fallback effective for zero-tail PMFs

statuses.title: Reject invalid and overflowing PLD composition counts

findings.title: b-min-sep MC transcripts are sharded by live Rayon thread count: fixed seed gives different epsilon on different hosts
findings.claim: The OPQ pattern fixed for balls-in-bins by closed issue #331 survives verbatim in the sibling b-min-sep Monte Carlo driver: bandmf_b_min_sep_prepare_transcripts and bandmf_b_min_sep_pld_from_transcripts partition num_samples by rayon::current_num_threads() and seed each chunk StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed + tid) / (seed + 1000 + tid), so the sampled transcript - and the resulting PLD and epsilon - depends on the machine's thread count.
findings.failure_scenario: A user calibrates a BandMF + b-min-sep run on an 8-core CI box and re-runs accounting with the same seed on a 16-core training host: the reported epsilon differs, golden-value tests flake across runners, and the documented fixed-seed reproducibility contract (which #550 restored for balls-in-bins with fixed-size seed-indexed shards) is silently broken for this mechanism.
evidence: mc.rs:174-176: 'let n_threads = rayon::current_num_threads().max(1); let samples_per_thread = num_samples / n_threads;' followed by per-tid 'StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed.wrapping_add(tid as u64))' (:187) and 'seed.wrapping_add(1000 + tid as u64)' (:210)

Reproduced with the built extension: _native.bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld([1.0,0.5], 8, 0.05, 1.0, cfg(seed=7)) gives delta_at(1.0) = 0.0073828822922578615 with RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1, 0.007361131568608619 with 4, 0.007696555912901023 with 8

Contrast with the fixed sibling: balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:46-54 uses fixed-size seed-indexed shards ('deterministic ... regardless of worker count') and has a thread-count-identity Rust test at :549
Not tracked by any open issue (checked issues-open.tsv; #666 covers regression vectors, #683/#688 cover horizon-prefix continuation)
findings.fix_sketch: Apply the same fix #550 applied to balls-in-bins: split sampling into fixed-size, seed-indexed shards (SAMPLES_PER_SHARD) processed with par_chunks_mut, with a shard_seed(seed, shard, direction) function independent of rayon::current_num_threads(); add a subprocess test mirroring tests/test_balls_in_bins_reproducible.py for bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld.

findings.title: Schedule-blind strategy equality lets the composition merge collapse distinct-lr-schedule MF processes
findings.claim: Residual of closed issue #332: all four MF strategy dataclasses declare lr_schedule as field(default=None, compare=False) (_band_mf.py:110, _bisr.py:160, _lambda_cgd.py:119, _blt.py:132), so MfGaussian.__eq__/__hash__ (plain dataclass semantics comparing the strategy field) are blind to the schedule, while the schedule genuinely changes the strategy's coefficients and sensitivity since #529. DpProcess.__or__'s same-leaf merge (opaque-accounting core/_base.py:474-477: 'if left_leaf == right_leaf: return Repeated(left_leaf, left_count + right_count)') therefore collapses two processes that differ only in lr_schedule into K repetitions of the LEFT one, silently pricing the second phase at the first phase's schedule.
findings.failure_scenario: A user composes two MF training phases with identical noise_multiplier/bands/momentum but different lr schedules (e.g. constant warmup phase then cosine decay): mf_gaussian(1.0, band_mf_strategy(bands=4, lr_schedule=s1)) | mf_gaussian(1.0, band_mf_strategy(bands=4, lr_schedule=s2)) becomes Repeated(phase1, 2); the reported epsilon corresponds to two copies of the s1-weighted sensitivity and can understate the true privacy loss when s2's weighting yields larger sensitivity. The PLD cache itself is NOT affected (its key materializes the schedule via strategy_cache_key), which makes the eq-path collapse easy to miss in cache-focused tests.
evidence: _band_mf.py:110: 'lr_schedule: Schedule | None = field(default=None, compare=False)' inside @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) BandMfStrategy - dataclass semantics exclude compare=False fields from __eq__ and __hash__
_band_mf.py:111-114: coefficients() passes _lr_key(self.lr_schedule, n_steps) into _band_mf_coefficients_cached, and sensitivity() is float(coefs.norm()) - the schedule changes the priced sensitivity
core/_base.py:474-477: '__or__' direct merge on 'left_leaf == right_leaf' returning Repeated(left_leaf, ...), discarding the right process object entirely
_mf_gaussian.py:41-75: MfGaussian is a default-eq frozen dataclass whose _pld_cache_key (but not __eq__) goes through strategy_cache_key/materialize_schedule (_schedule_fingerprint.py:12-43)
findings.fix_sketch: Either include a schedule fingerprint in strategy equality (e.g. drop compare=False and compare a materialization-stable token, or give the strategies a custom __eq__ that compares _lr_key at the declared horizon), or make DpProcess.__or__'s merge use _pld_cache_key-style resolved identity instead of dataclass __eq__ for leaves that defer resolution.

findings.title: Closed #338 landed no change: asymmetric PLD metrics still renormalize negative-infinity mass away, inconsistently with the symmetric path
findings.claim: No commit in 79c916e3..4b13d82 touches negative_infinity_mass handling in pld/metrics.rs (git log -S confirms; the closest commits are #466, which only exposes infinity_mass, and #283, docs/labels). The symmetric trade-off pmf_beta floors the Y-CDF with negative_infinity_mass to keep beta conservative (metrics.rs:212-216), while pmf_beta_asymmetric deliberately drops it via clean_probs renormalization (metrics.rs:305 'No negative_infinity_mass: it's absorbed by the renormalization', :314 'No negative_infinity_mass added') - the exact inconsistency the closed issue title names.
findings.failure_scenario: beta_at/risk_at on an asymmetric PLD carrying negative_infinity_mass (random_allocation.rs:157-185,250 and connect_the_dots.rs:278 both build new_asymmetric PLDs, and composition adds the left Chernoff tail budget to negative_infinity_mass in dense.rs) redistributes the -inf mass proportionally over the finite grid instead of treating it as mass at -infinity; the resulting beta/risk differs from the conservative symmetric treatment by up to that mass. Magnitude is bounded by the tail budget (~1e-15 analytic default), so practical impact is negligible today, but the guarantee direction is unaudited and the two paths disagree by construction.
evidence: metrics.rs:212-216: symmetric path 'cdf_y[0] = pmf.negative_infinity_mass + pmf.probs[0]' with comment 'keeping beta estimates conservative'
metrics.rs:305: asymmetric path comment 'No negative_infinity_mass: it's absorbed by the renormalization to sum(probs) = 1 - infinity_mass (matching riskcal)'

git log -S negative_infinity_mass 79c916e3..4b13d82 -- packages/opaque-accounting/src/pld returns only #528 (composition-side budgets) and #307 (feature); metrics.rs delta commits are #466 and #283 only
findings.fix_sketch: Either fold negative_infinity_mass into the asymmetric CDF the same way the symmetric path does (with a derivation of the conservative direction for the symmetrized trade-off), or document the riskcal-matching renormalization as the deliberate resolution and record the bounded error; in both cases the closed issue should be reopened or annotated since its titled reconciliation never landed.

findings.title: Trainer accountant.json save crashes with RecursionError for composition spines deeper than ~1000
findings.claim: Residual of closed issue #334: the codec, equality, hash and repr are fully iterative (verified at depth 3000), but the wire format is a nested dict mirroring the spine, so json.dump(opaque_state_dict(accountant), f) at the trainer checkpoint path recurses once per spine level and raises RecursionError beyond the default recursionlimit (~1000).
findings.failure_scenario: A training run whose per-step processes do not merge (heterogeneous step parameters, e.g. a per-step-varying noise multiplier or mixed mechanisms composed with |) accumulates a Composed spine one node per step; at checkpoint save the accountant serializes fine but json.dump crashes, aborting the save. Homogeneous default loops are unaffected because __or__ collapses identical steps into a single Repeated node. Fail-closed (a crash, not silent corruption), but it can lose a checkpoint mid-run.
evidence: Reproduced in this session: 3000-deep heterogeneous Composed spine -> state_dict/hash/repr/eq/round-trip all OK, then json.dumps(state_dict(Accountant(prefix=proc))) raised RecursionError (recursionlimit 1000)
_process_codec.py:27-70 emits nested dict slots ('stack.append((v, slot))  # iterate, don't recurse') - iterative construction of a recursively-shaped payload
_dp_trainer.py:4995: 'json.dump(opaque_state_dict(accountant), f)' writes accountant.json
findings.fix_sketch: Emit spines as a flat list on the wire (e.g. {'type':'ComposedSpine','nodes':[...]}) or serialize with an iterative JSON encoder; alternatively cap/normalize spine depth by folding runs into Repeated nodes before serialization.
